dedupe_keys.name: flaps farm location and agricultural production simulator simulated us swine farms

description: FLAPS is a spatial microsimulation model that simulates the location and populations of individual livestock farms across the conterminous United States, and this Dryad deposit gives its data for domestic pig farms. The DataCite record says livestock can otherwise only be mapped at county level or coarser, and that the authors fitted iterative proportional-fitting algorithms to the hierarchical US Census of Agriculture, imputed state and county totals withheld for confidentiality, and used a weighted sample of farm locations to predict where farms sit. It was published on 19 October 2016 by Christopher Burdett, Brian Kraus, Sarah Garza, Ryan Miller and Kathe Bjork as downloadable files of about 1.2 MB, free under CC0 1.0, with national coverage of the conterminous US. Caveats: farm points are simulated, not real addresses, only swine are covered in this deposit, and the census year behind it is not stated on the page read. For simulation it gives farm-level livestock locations for disease spread and agent-based outbreak models, and for exposure of livestock to floods, heat and feed or power supply disruptions. Related catalogue records include the global livestock distribution 1 km data, FAO Gridded Livestock of the World and the USDA June survey data.
